sections.label: COVID-19 support and recovery
sections.summary: Close to $100 billion was committed over two years to cushion COVID-19 effects, with unemployment at 3.2% and median income up around 1% in real terms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We worked together to cushion the effects of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We committed close to $100 billion over the past two years to support Singaporeans and businesses through the uncertainties of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The resident unemployment rate has come down to 3.2%, close to pre-COVID-19 levels.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The median income of full-time employed residents grew by around 1% in real terms last year, after a decline of 0.4% in 2020.

sections.label: Jobs and Business Support Package
sections.summary: A $500 million Jobs and Business Support Package gives eligible SMEs $1,000 per local employee, capped at $10,000 per firm, amid 3% to 5% growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our economy should grow by 3% to 5% this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: While the overall outlook is positive, I recognise that there are still segments of the economy that are still struggling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will therefore provide targeted help for our workers and businesses in these sectors, through a $500 million Jobs and Business Support Package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: SMEs in the eligible sectors will receive a payout of $1,000 per local employee, up to a cap of $10,000 per firm.

sections.label: MAS exchange rate band tightening
sections.summary: MAS raised the rate of appreciation of its exchange rate policy band in October last year and again last month to dampen inflationary pressures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are also seeing the effects of the expansionary macro-economic policies pursued by the US and other developed countries to revive their economies following the onset of the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is why the MAS had taken the pre-emptive step of raising the rate of appreciation of its exchange rate policy band in October last year and again, last month, to help dampen inflationary pressures.

sections.label: Loan scheme extensions
sections.summary: The Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and enhanced Trade Loan Scheme are extended six months, and Project Loans for domestic construction one year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To support companies with their cashflow needs, I will extend the Temporary Bridging Loan Programme and the enhanced Trade Loan Scheme, with revised parameters, for another six months, from 1 April to 30 September this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will also extend access to Project Loans for the domestic construction sector for another year, from 1 April this year to 31 March next year.

sections.label: GST Voucher U-Save rebates
sections.summary: GST Voucher U-Save rebates are doubled for the rest of this year, with eligible HDB households receiving additional rebates of up to $285.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As part of the Package, I will double the GST Voucher – U-Save rebates for the rest of this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Eligible HDB households will receive additional rebates of up to $285.

sections.label: Utility, education and essentials package
sections.summary: The measures amount to a $560 million package to help Singaporeans with utility bills, children's education and daily essentials.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: All these amount to a significant package of $560 million to help Singaporeans with their utility bills, children’s education and daily essentials.

sections.label: Local worker income inequality
sections.summary: Real incomes of local workers at the 20th percentile rose almost 40% from 2009 to 2019, and inequality after taxes and transfers improved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Real incomes of our local workers at the 20th percentile have risen by almost 40% between 2009 and 2019, faster than that of the median worker.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Lower-income workers have also benefited from our highly progressive system of taxes and transfers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Inequality after taxes and transfers as measured by the Gini coefficient has steadily improved over the last decade.

sections.label: Singapore ageing population
sections.summary: In 2010, 9% of the population were aged 65 and above; by 2030, 25% of Singaporeans are expected to be 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In 2010, 9% of our population were aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: By 2030, we expect Singapore to become like Japan and some European countries today – where one in four or 25% of Singaporeans will be 65 and above.

sections.label: Net zero emissions cost
sections.summary: Moving to net zero emissions will be very costly for Singapore, a built-up city-state with limited scope for renewable energies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Moving to net zero emissions will be a very costly affair for Singapore, a built-up city-state with very limited scope to tap on renewable energies.

sections.label: Government spending and GDP
sections.summary: Government spending today, excluding COVID-19-related expenditure, stands at $88 billion, about 18% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Government spending today, excluding COVID-19-related expenditure, stands at $88 billion, or about 18% of GDP.

sections.label: NIRC revenue stream
sections.summary: Over the past five years, NIRC provided an average revenue stream of around $17 billion, about 3.5% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, NIRC provided on average a revenue stream of around $17 billion or about 3.5% of GDP.

sections.label: Social spending increase
sections.summary: Social spending almost doubled from $17 billion to $31 billion over the last decade and now takes up close to half of the annual Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our social spending in particular, has almost doubled from $17 billion to $31 billion over the last decade and now takes up close to half of our annual Budget.

sections.label: Government spending and healthcare
sections.summary: By 2030, Government expenditures are expected to exceed 20% of GDP, with most of the increase going to healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: By 2030, we expect Government expenditures to increase to more than 20% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Most of this increase in spending will go to healthcare.

sections.label: Slower growth constrains tax revenues
sections.summary: Slowing labour force and GDP growth will constrain tax revenues, so the Budget will make significant enhancements to the tax system.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But our sharply slowing labour force growth and hence, slower GDP growth compared to the last decade, will constrain our tax revenues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is why we will make significant enhancements to our tax system in this Budget.

sections.label: Budget goals and key changes
sections.summary: The Budget aims to give Singaporeans confidence to embrace change and sets out changes to invest, go green, strengthen the social compact and develop a fairer revenue structure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It is about giving Singaporeans the confidence to embrace the change that lies before us, so that we can grow into an ever stronger economy and nation, and an ever more secure society and home.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This Budget will set out the key changes we must make to: (a)	invest in new capabilities; (b)	advance our green transition; (c)	renew and strengthen our social compact; and (d)	develop a fairer and more resilient revenue structure.

sections.label: Investing in broadband and digital capabilities
sections.summary: Broadband access speeds will be upgraded about 10 times, future technologies like 6G will be invested in, and $200 million will enhance digital capability schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will invest further to meet our future needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will upgrade our broadband infrastructure to increase broadband access speeds by around 10 times over the next few years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will also invest in future technologies like 6G, to ride the next communications and connectivity wave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Alongside infrastructure improvements, I will set aside an additional $200 million over the next few years to enhance schemes that build digital capabilities in our businesses and workers.

sections.label: Sustaining R&D investment
sections.summary: Government investment in R&D has been maintained at about 1% of GDP, with $25 billion set aside under the RIE2025 strategy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why, over the years, we have steadily increased the Government’s investment in R&D, maintaining it at about 1% of GDP, comparable to other small advanced economies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: I will continue to sustain our investments in R&D, with $25 billion set aside under the Research, Innovation and Enterprise, or RIE2025 strategy.

sections.label: Local enterprises and business R&D
sections.summary: Local enterprises make up about 80% of all firms but account for only about a quarter of total business R&D expenditure in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Local enterprises, which comprise about 80% of all firms, account for only about a quarter of total business R&D expenditure in Singapore.

sections.label: Innovation projects in pilot sectors
sections.summary: Over five years, these centres will undertake close to 2,000 innovation projects across five pilot sectors, an eight-fold increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Over the next five years, these centres will be able to undertake close to 2,000 innovation projects across five pilot sectors: Agri-Tech, Construction, Food Manufacturing, Precision Engineering and Retail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This amounts to an eight-fold increase in the number of innovation projects undertaken in these sectors.

sections.label: PSG and Singapore Global Enterprises
sections.summary: SMEs can use the PSG, with around $600 million set aside to expand solutions and support over 100,000 productivity projects; larger local enterprises get Singapore Global Enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: SMEs can make use of the Productivity Solutions Grant, or PSG, to implement digital and automation solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will set aside around $600 million to expand the range of available solutions under the PSG and push for greater take up of productivity solutions by SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We estimate that this will support more than 100,000 productivity projects over the next four years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Larger local enterprises need more customised assistance to scale up and invest in overseas markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will support them with a new initiative called Singapore Global Enterprises.

sections.label: Skills Development Levy waiver
sections.summary: A Skills Development Levy waiver is granted for 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2021, estimated to double eligible employers from 40,000 to 80,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To better support our smaller and micro enterprises, I will grant a waiver of the Skills Development Levy requirement for the qualifying period of 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This is estimated to double the number of eligible employers, from 40,000 today to 80,000.

sections.label: NTUC company training committees
sections.summary: To date, NTUC has formed more than 800 CTCs with companies of various sizes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To date, NTUC has formed more than 800 CTCs with companies of various sizes.

sections.label: Funding to scale up CTCs
sections.summary: About $100 million is set aside to support NTUC in scaling up CTCs, part going to a new NTUC-administered grant for companies with CTCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Through the support of the CTC, he has acquired new skills and will be well positioned to excel in his career.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will therefore set aside about $100 million to support NTUC in its efforts to scale up the CTCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Part of this will go into a new grant which will be administered by NTUC, to support companies that have set up CTCs to implement their transformation plans.

sections.label: Mid-career training and SkillsFuture programme
sections.summary: Company attachments for mature mid-career workers under the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme become permanent, with a new SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Under the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme, we have provided company attachments for mid-career workers to undergo skills upgrading with a training allowance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will make such company attachments for mature mid-career workers a permanent feature of our training and placement ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In recent years and especially during the pandemic, we have significantly expanded such training opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will continue to enhance our provision of high-quality, industry-oriented training courses through a new SkillsFuture Career Transition Programme.

sections.label: Employment Pass salary threshold raised
sections.summary: From September, the minimum qualifying salary for new Employment Pass applicants rises from $4,500 to $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will aim to ensure that incoming EP holders are comparable in quality to the top one-third of our local PMET workforce, those with professional, managerial, executive and technical jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Therefore, from September this year, the minimum qualifying salary for new EP applicants will be raised from the current $4,500 to $5,000.

sections.label: S Pass salary thresholds raised
sections.summary: From September, the minimum qualifying salary for new S Pass applicants rises from $2,500 to $3,000, and to $3,500 for financial services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In the first step, we will raise the minimum qualifying salary for new S Pass applicants from the current $2,500 to $3,000 in September this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will introduce a higher minimum qualifying salary of $3,500 for the financial services sector.

sections.label: S Pass levy and quota changes
sections.summary: From 1 January 2024, the Tier 1 levy rises to $650 by 2025, the DRC falls to 1:5, and the MYE framework is replaced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To better manage the flow of S Pass holders, we will progressively raise the Tier 1 levy from the current $330 to $650 by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Dependency Ratio Ceiling, or DRC, will be reduced from the current 1:7 to 1:5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The current Man-Year Entitlement, or MYE, framework will be replaced with a new levy framework that will encourage firms to support more offsite work and employ more higher-skilled work permit holders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And to give companies time to prepare for the moves, these changes will take effect from 1 January 2024.

sections.label: Carbon tax increases
sections.summary: The carbon tax rises to $25 per tonne in 2024 and 2025, $45 in 2026 and 2027, aiming for $50 to $80 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To move decisively to achieve our new net zero ambition, we will need a higher carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will therefore raise our carbon tax to $25 per tonne in 2024 and 2025 and $45 per tonne in 2026 and 2027, with a view to reaching $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The current tax of $5 per tonne will remain unchanged until 2023, as previously stated.

sections.label: Transition framework for firms
sections.summary: A transition framework will be put in place to support firms needing more time to cut emissions or invest in cleaner technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Some will need a little more time to make the necessary reduction in emissions or investment in cleaner technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, to support such firms and manage the near-term impact on their competitiveness, we will put in place a transition framework.

sections.label: International carbon credits offset
sections.summary: From 2024, businesses may use high-quality international carbon credits to offset up to 5% of taxable emissions instead of paying carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: From 2024, we will also allow businesses to use high-quality, international carbon credits to offset up to 5% of their taxable emissions, in lieu of paying carbon tax.

sections.label: Carbon price utility bill impact
sections.summary: A $25 per tonne carbon price would raise an average 4-room HDB household's utility bills by about $4 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At $25 per tonne, this would translate to an increase of about $4 per month in the utility bills for an average 4-room HDB household.

sections.label: Public sector green bonds
sections.summary: The public sector aims to issue up to $35 billion of green bonds by 2030, publish a Singapore Green Bond Framework and issue an inaugural green bond this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The public sector will do its part to develop a robust green finance market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We aim to issue up to $35 billion of green bonds by 2030 to fund public sector green infrastructure projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Government will also publish a Singapore Green Bond Framework and issue its inaugural green bond later this year.

sections.label: Phasing out combustion engine vehicles
sections.summary: The Government announced its intention to phase out internal combustion engine vehicles by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For those who wish to drive, we want their vehicles to be cleaner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Hence, we had announced our intention to phase out internal combustion engine vehicles by 2040.

sections.label: EV adoption and charging points
sections.summary: EV share of new car registrations rose from 0.2% in 2020 to around 4% last year, and more charging points will be built closer to homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In fact, within a year, the EV share of new car registrations has jumped from just 0.2% in 2020 to around 4% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Given this momentum, we will further accelerate EV adoption by building more charging points closer to where we live.

sections.label: Lower-wage worker recommendations implemented
sections.summary: The Government will implement Tripartite Workgroup recommendations, extending the Progressive Wage Model to retail, food services and waste management, requiring foreign-worker firms to pay locals at least $1,400, and requiring eligible suppliers to be PW Mark accredited from March 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Government has accepted and will implement the recommendations of the Tripartite Workgroup on Lower-Wage Workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, over the next two years, we will extend the Progressive Wage Model to the retail, food services, and waste management sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Companies employing foreign workers will be required to pay all their local employees at least the Local Qualifying Salary, which is currently set at $1,400 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The Government will require all our eligible suppliers to be accredited with the PW Mark when they contract with us from March 2023.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme
sections.summary: The PWCS will co-fund lower-wage worker wage increases from 2022 to 2026, with co-funding rates of 50%, 30% then 15%, starting with a $2 billion fund injection this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Others may find it difficult to raise prices in the short term to support the wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will therefore introduce the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme, or PWCS, to provide transitional support for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Under the PWCS, the Government will co-fund the wage increases of lower-wage workers between 2022 and 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For workers earning up to $2,500, the PWCS co-funding rate will be 50% in the first two years, 30% in the next two years, before tapering to 15% in 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: With this, the Government will be co-sharing with employers a significant portion of the cost increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will set up a PWCS fund for this purpose and start with a $2 billion injection this year.

sections.label: Qualifying income cap raised
sections.summary: From 1 January 2023, the qualifying income cap will rise from $2,300 to $2,500 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: From 1 January 2023, I will raise the qualifying income cap from the current $2,300 to $2,500 per month.

sections.label: PWCS and Workfare spending
sections.summary: An average of $1.8 billion per year over five years, or $9 billion total, will be spent on PWCS and enhanced Workfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In aggregate, we will spend an average of $1.8 billion per year over the next five years, or $9 billion in total for the PWCS and the enhanced Workfare.

sections.label: KidSTART support target
sections.summary: KidSTART is on track to support 5,000 children by 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: KidSTART is on track to support 5,000 children by 2023.

sections.label: UPLIFT Community Network expansion
sections.summary: The pilot will expand into a nationwide UPLIFT Community Network, starting with eight additional towns this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The pilot has yielded positive outcomes, with school attendance improving for most of the students placed on the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we will expand the pilot into a nationwide UPLIFT Community Network to benefit more students, starting with eight additional towns this year and more in the coming years.

sections.label: ComLink social service integration
sections.summary: Social services will be integrated and Community Link scaled up to support lower-income families with children in rental housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will therefore integrate the delivery of our social services to more effectively uplift lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will do so as we scale up Community Link, or ComLink, which provides targeted support for families with children living in rental housing.

sections.label: Healthcare expenditure projection
sections.summary: Government healthcare expenditure tripled from $3.7 billion in 2010 to $11.3 billion in 2019, and could reach about $27 billion by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Government healthcare expenditure has already tripled from $3.7 billion in 2010 to $11.3 billion in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: If our current healthcare expenditure, excluding COVID-19-related expenditure, continues to increase at a similar rate over the coming decade, we will spend about $27 billion or around 3.5% of GDP by 2030.

sections.label: Healthcare IT integration
sections.summary: Healthcare IT systems will be integrated so information flows beyond hospitals to community healthcare providers, under the Healthier SG strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will also need to integrate our healthcare IT systems so that information can flow beyond hospitals to community healthcare providers, to enable quality care and maximise convenience to patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are thinking through this “Healthier SG” strategy carefully.

sections.label: Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health
sections.summary: An Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being was established to coordinate public agencies and integrate community mental health and social services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We want to make sure that the lessons learnt are embedded into our healthcare and social support system, in a sustainable and permanent manner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Therefore, we have established an Interagency Taskforce on Mental Health and Well-being to coordinate efforts across public agencies and other stakeholders, and to enhance and integrate mental health and social services in the community.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan 2030
sections.summary: The Enabling Masterplan 2030 will be launched later this year to strengthen support in employment, lifelong learning and respite care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Later this year, we will launch the Enabling Masterplan 2030 to further strengthen support in areas like employment, lifelong learning and respite care.

sections.label: Tote Board fund-raising support
sections.summary: A $100 million top-up will extend Government support for Tote Board's Enhanced Fund-Raising Programme for three years until end-FY2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To provide more support for the charity sector and to encourage giving, I will provide a top-up of $100 million to extend the Government’s support for Tote Board’s Enhanced Fund-Raising Programme for three years until end-FY2024.

sections.label: Cultural Matching Fund top-up
sections.summary: A $150 million top-up over three years will support the Cultural Matching Fund, which matches donations to Arts and Heritage charities dollar-for-dollar.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To further encourage cultural philanthropy, I will provide a top-up of $150 million to the Cultural Matching Fund for three years, which provides dollar-for-dollar matching for donations made to Arts and Heritage charities.

sections.label: Pillar 2 global minimum tax
sections.summary: Pillar 2 sets a 15% global minimum effective tax rate for large MNE groups, and Singapore is exploring a Minimum Effective Tax Rate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Pillar 2 introduces, amongst other things, a global minimum effective tax rate of 15% for MNE groups with annual global revenues of 750 million euros or more, under its Global Anti-Base Erosion or GloBE Model Rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will adjust our tax system in response to Pillar 2 GloBE rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are exploring a top-up tax called the Minimum Effective Tax Rate, or “METR”.

sections.label: Top personal income tax rates
sections.summary: The top marginal personal income tax rate rises from 22% to 23% and 24% for chargeable income above $500,000 and $1 million from Year of Assessment 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Where personal income tax is concerned, there is room for greater progressivity, so that those who earn more, contribute more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will therefore increase the top marginal personal income tax, or PIT rate with effect from the Year of Assessment 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The portion of chargeable income in excess of $500,000 up to $1 million will be taxed at 23%, while that in excess of $1 million will be taxed at 24%; both up from 22% today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This increase is expected to affect the top 1.2% of personal income taxpayers and will raise $170 million of additional tax revenue per year.

sections.label: Non-owner-occupied property tax rates
sections.summary: Property tax rates for such properties increase from the current 10% to 20% range to 12% to 36%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For such properties, I will increase the property tax rates from 10% to 20% which is the current range, to 12% to 36%.

sections.label: Owner-occupied property tax rates
sections.summary: Property tax rates for owner-occupied residential properties rise from 4% to 16% to 6% to 32% for Annual Value above $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For owner-occupied residential properties, I will increase the property tax rates for the portion of Annual Value in excess of $30,000, from today’s 4% to 16%, to 6% to 32%.

sections.label: GST increase and offsets
sections.summary: GST rises from 7% to 8% on 1 January 2023 and to 9% on 1 January 2024, with offsets for healthcare, education, Town Councils and a one-year freeze on Government fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The first increase will take place on 1 January 2023 from 7% to 8%, and the second increase on 1 January 2024 from 8% to 9%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will continue to absorb GST on publicly subsidised healthcare and education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will provide Town Councils with an additional $15 million per year to absorb the additional GST payable on Service and Conservancy Charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will not increase Government fees and charges for one year from 1 January 2023.

sections.label: Anti-profiteering committee and Assurance Package
sections.summary: A Committee Against Profiteering will be set up, and the $6 billion Assurance Package gets an additional $640 million top-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To address concerns that businesses could use GST as a cover to raise prices, the Government will stand up a Committee Against Profiteering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We had earlier announced a $6 billion Assurance Package to cushion the impact of the GST increase for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will provide an additional top-up of $640 million to the Assurance Package.

sections.label: GSTV Cash payout changes
sections.summary: The GSTV Cash Assessable Income threshold rises from $28,000 to $34,000, and payouts increase to $500 and $250 based on home Annual Values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Second, the Assessable Income threshold for GSTV – Cash will increase from $28,000 to $34,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Third, I will increase the quantum of the GSTV – Cash payout to $500 for those residing in homes with Annual Values of $13,000 and below; and to $250, for those residing in homes with Annual Values of between $13,000 and $21,000.

sections.label: COVID-19 Past Reserves draw
sections.summary: Singapore expected to use $31.9 billion from Past Reserves for COVID-19 relief in FY2020, lower than the $52 billion initially planned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At the onset of COVID-19 in FY2020, we were looking to draw up to $52 billion from Past Reserves to protect lives and livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Given the uncertainty of the crisis at that time, we had to set aside sufficient resources to handle any downside scenarios.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We now expect to utilise a lower amount of $31.9 billion from Past Reserves for COVID-19 relief in FY2020.

sections.label: FY2021 Past Reserves draw
sections.summary: For FY2021, Singapore now expects to draw $5 billion from Past Reserves for the COVID-19 Resilience Package, lower than the planned $11 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For FY2021, we had planned to draw up to $11 billion from Past Reserves for the COVID-19 Resilience Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We now expect to draw a lower amount of $5 billion from Past Reserves.

sections.label: President's support for draw
sections.summary: The President has given in-principle support, bringing total expected draw on past reserves from FY2020 to FY2022 to up to $42.9 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The President has given her in-principle support for this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This brings the total expected draw on past reserves over FY2020 to FY2022 to up to $42.9 billion.

sections.label: Further 1% budget cut
sections.summary: From FY2023, a further 1% cut will be applied to the budgets of Ministries and Organs of State.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: From FY2023, I will apply a further 1% cut to the budgets of Ministries and Organs of State.

sections.label: FY2022 expansionary Budget deficit
sections.summary: For FY2022, the Budget remains expansionary, with an expected overall deficit of $3 billion or 0.5% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For FY2022, our Budget remains expansionary to support the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I expect an overall deficit of $3 billion or 0.5% of GDP.

sections.label: Frontline workers and partnerships
sections.summary: The speaker remembers frontline workers' courage and how public and private groups set up Community Care Facilities at the Expo in 2020, and later Singapore Together projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will never forget the contributions of our frontline warriors – how they displayed tremendous courage, valiantly took on personal risks to fight the virus, and went above and beyond the call of duty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I will always remember how different groups from the public and private sectors joined forces to set up the Community Care Facilities at the Expo in 2020, when we were overwhelmed with our first wave of infection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: They worked hand in hand and against all odds, got the facility up and running in a matter of days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Since then, we have launched many more “Singapore Together” projects, involving public-private partnerships and Alliances for Action.

sections.label: Fans' spirit at football match
sections.summary: Fans stayed after a lost semi-final, applauded the team, and spontaneously sang the National Anthem together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In these difficult times, many looked beyond their own circumstances to help others in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I saw this same resilient spirit at the AFF Suzuki Cup semi-final football match last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Even though they lost the game in extra-time, many fans stayed on after the match and applauded the team, proud of how they had persevered despite going down to eight men.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: At the end, the fans in the stadium stood at attention and everyone started singing the National Anthem in unison spontaneously.

sections.label: Budget debate adjourned
sections.summary: The debate on approving the Government's financial policy for 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2023 stands adjourned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That Parliament approves the financial policy of the Government for the financial year 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2023." In accordance with paragraph (1) of Standing Order No 89, the debate now stands adjourned.
